title: Perform a Mini Accessibility Audit
description: Evaluate a real webpage using automated tools and manual checks, then document three findings.
problemStatement:
## Mini Audit

Pick a public website (e.g., a local library, a small restaurant site). Perform the following:

1. Run axe DevTools on the home page. Note any violations (type, severity).
2. Manually test:
   - Tab through the entire page. Is focus visible and logical? Any keyboard traps?
   - Zoom to 200%. Does content reflow without horizontal scroll?
   - Check colour contrast of the main heading and one button using a contrast checker.
3. Use a screen reader (VoiceOver or NVDA) to navigate:
   - Listen to the heading structure.
   - Navigate by landmarks.
   - Try to fill out a form (if any).

Write a short report with 3 issues you found, including:
- Location/description
- WCAG criterion violated (look it up if needed)
- Severity
- Suggested fix

Submit the report as plain text or a document.
hints: If axe reports 'No issues', dig deeper with manual tests – there are always subtle problems.
For screen reader, note any links or buttons that are announced as 'blank' or just 'button'.
expectedOutput: A brief audit report with three documented findings.
solutionCode:
Example finding:
1. Location: Navigation bar, 'About' link.
   Issue: The link text is 'About' but the adjacent 'About' in footer is identical – could be confusing out of context. (Not critical, but better as 'About Us' and 'About Our Mission'?)
   WCAG: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) – actually fine if context clear, but consider.

Real issue: Form input 'Name' has no label, only placeholder. WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; fix with <label for='name'>Name</label>.
